transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Rinaldi (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Verdant CTO), Alex Gomez (Verdant ML Eng), Dana Ortiz (Verdant Head of Security)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on PLG/self-serve onboarding, free credits, and time-to-first-token. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PHI-adjacent triage/summarization product. Discussed integration path, security controls, and cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:00 Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, Jordan here from Redwood, joining with Sofia from our engineering side, how's everyone doing?
00:07 Priya Menon: good thanks, a bit slammed end of year but excited to chat, appreciate you fitting us in
00:12 Alex Gomez: same, quick note we're evaluating a couple vendors but wanted to see the self-serve flow and how fast we can get a POC up
00:20 Sofia Rinaldi: awesome, we'll cover quickstart, credits, and the typical path to first token; also happy to dig into perf/infra if you want
00:28 Dana Ortiz: and I'll jump in on security questions, SOC2, KMS, data retention, that kind of stuff

01:02 Jordan Park: quick qualification — what's your current stack for models and infra? you running anything on-prem or cloud?
01:12 Priya Menon: we're mostly on GCP, internal infra for PHI is isolated in VPC, we currently call OpenAI for non-sensitive workloads; for sensitive triage and summarization we need either dedicated tenancy or private deployment
01:30 Alex Gomez: our typical requests are 1k-4k token chat summarization and triage; latency target is sub-500ms tail for user-facing UI, but backend batch can tolerate higher latency if cost savings are significant
01:48 Sofia Rinaldi: ok good context — for quickstart hosted API we can get you tokens in minutes, we also have Dedicated reserved capacity and Private deployment for VPC/on-prem which meet stricter isolation. are you leaning one way?
02:03 Priya Menon: preference is try hosted for dev/fast iteration, but we need confirm around data residency and ability to opt into Private for prod if compliance requires

03:10 Dana Ortiz: do you have SOC2 and how do you handle encryption and KMS? we need audit logs and separation of keys for prod workloads
03:22 Jordan Park: yes SOC2 Type II, we provide KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys for Private; hosted has encryption at rest with controlled key management, we can share the security docs after call
03:35 Dana Ortiz: ok please share the SOC2 report and the KMS integration doc

05:00 Alex Gomez: practical question — how fast to first token if we use the self-serve API? can one of your engineers walk me through a sample curl flow or SDK?
05:10 Sofia Rinaldi: absolutely — typical flow is sign up, create API key, run quickstart repo, call text-generation endpoint. for most teams it's under 30 minutes if you have network access. we give starter credits that you can apply to the account
05:25 Priya Menon: what size are starter credits usually? we want to be able to run a couple hundred regen calls and a small benchmark
05:33 Jordan Park: default trial is $500 — but for qualifying teams we can allocate up to $5k to run initial benchmarks; we'll confirm based on scope

07:00 Alex Gomez: and on model catalog — do you host open models or proprietary ones? we want something high-quality for summarization but also options to optimize cost with quantized variants
07:12 Sofia Rinaldi: we host a catalog of open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles; also have quantized variants for cost/latency tradeoffs. we can route requests to cheaper variants or fall back to higher-cap models for critical requests
07:28 Alex Gomez: sounds good. curious about batching and KV caching — do you do automatic prefix caching?
07:36 Sofia Rinaldi: yes automatic prefix/KV caching is part of the runtime; it depends on usage patterns but you'll often see strong token-cost wins for chat-heavy flows

09:00 Priya Menon: you mentioned Dedicated — if we pivot to Dedicated later, what's the procurement cadence and typical lead time?
09:12 Jordan Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; lead time varies but typically weeks for allocation if using cloud-backed Dedicated. Private (VPC/on-prem) takes longer, often a few months depending on compliance and setup
09:30 Dana Ortiz: for Private, do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? and can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
09:36 Sofia Rinaldi: yes to both; we support customer KMS integrations and log forwarding. we'll share the architecture doc and SIEM integration notes

11:15 Alex Gomez: any known limitations on token length for hosted? we want to run 8k and 16k sequences for some pipelines
11:23 Sofia Rinaldi: hosted supports longer context models but check model-specific limits in the catalog. for very long sequences we sometimes recommend dedicated nodes with memory-optimized configs or quantized backends
11:40 Alex Gomez: and cost delta vs. OpenAI? ballpark per-token?
11:46 Jordan Park: depends on model; our catalog has price tiers. often competitive with large providers, especially when you optimize with batching, caching, and quantized variants. we'll share a pricing comparison spreadsheet

14:00 Priya Menon: security is blocker for prod, but we want to prototype ASAP. what's the path to do a dev-only hosted POC and then migrate to Private if needed?
14:12 Jordan Park: standard path — self-serve hosted quickstart for dev, can scope a pilot on Dedicated if you want predictable throughput, and Private is next step for compliance. we support pinning model versions and rollout policies to make the migration safe
14:30 Dana Ortiz: will onboarding to Private require an SLA and legal review?
14:36 Jordan Park: yes Private/custom contracts typically have enterprise agreements and support/SLAs; procurement/legal will engage once you decide to proceed

17:00 Alex Gomez: let's do a quick live demo of the quickstart flow — Sofia?
17:05 Sofia Rinaldi: sure, I'll share screen — starting the quickstart repo, we have a one-file example using our SDK. first step: pip install redwood-client, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, here's the sample curl...
17:37 Sofia Rinaldi: (screen) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-small-8k","input":"Summarize the following..."}'
18:00 Alex Gomez: ok so that's straightforward, any gotchas with network/inbound egress for our VPC?
18:08 Sofia Rinaldi: for hosted you need outbound access to our API endpoints; for stricter networks we can use Private or Dedicated with VPC peering or private links

20:00 Priya Menon: cost controls — can you set per-key quotas, rate limits, and alerting? we need to avoid runaway charges during experiments
20:12 Jordan Park: yes per-key quotas, rate-limiting, and usage alerts in Console; you can also set routing policies to prefer cheaper model variants for non-critical requests

22:30 Dana Ortiz: compliance — retention and deletion policies? can you ensure customer-data deletion on request?
22:40 Jordan Park: yes we have configurable retention, deletion APIs, and audit logs. for Private deployments you can fully isolate logs and apply your retention policies

25:00 Alex Gomez: one more perf question — do you expose token-level latency breakdowns? we'd like to see where time is spent: kernel, I/O, batching
25:12 Sofia Rinaldi: Console gives token-level cost/latency, per-route dashboards and traces; SE can help instrument a few calls so you can see breakdowns live

28:00 Priya Menon: ok sounds promising. what's the recommended first experiment?
28:10 Jordan Park: recommended: 1) sign up and run quickstart on hosted with a small workload; 2) run our benchmark script against 1k/4k/8k sequences; 3) share results and we'll propose Dedicated/Private sizing if needed

30:00 Alex Gomez: timeline — we want pilot running in Jan, timeline looks reasonable?
30:08 Jordan Park: yes if you get us a sample dataset and confirm scope we can provision credits and benchmark in the first week of Jan

32:00 Priya Menon: can you send an example contract for Dedicated procurement so legal can eyeball?
32:12 Jordan Park: yes I can share a redline-friendly template and the SOW we've used with other health customers

34:00 Dana Ortiz: please include data processing addendum and SOC2 in that packet
34:08 Jordan Park: will do

36:00 Sofia Rinaldi: quick technical note — for triage workloads where latency is critical we recommend model variants tuned for low tail latency and aggressive prefix caching; we'll show sample configs in the benchmark spreadsheet
36:18 Alex Gomez: great. any known integration issues with GCP?
36:24 Sofia Rinaldi: nothing major; for Private we can deploy into your VPC and attach to your KMS; for hosted, just egress to our endpoints

38:00 Jordan Park: to recap next steps: we'll allocate trial credits (potentially $5k), send quickstart guide, SOC2 and KMS docs, pricing comparison, and Dedicated contract template. Sofia will run a perf benchmark plan once Alex shares sample data
38:20 Priya Menon: sounds good, thanks. Alex will drop the sample dataset to Slack
38:30 Alex Gomez: yeah I'll share by EOD tomorrow

40:00 Dana Ortiz: one last question — do you have any reference customers in healthcare who've done Private deployments?
40:08 Jordan Park: yes we've worked with a couple of health customers; I'll include redacted references in the packet

42:00 Priya Menon: ok thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll follow up after Alex shares the data
42:10 Jordan Park: great — we'll follow through on action items. appreciate the time

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional auto-transcribe errors, speaker labels approximate. Shared artifacts: quickstart repo (link shared in chat), security packet (to be emailed), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared by Sofia).
